key_themes: Chip sector rout triggered by CXMT (China DRAM maker) IPO and SK Hynix -15% crash in Korea
Big Tech earnings week with MSFT, AMZN, AAPL, META reporting later this week; Fed decision due Wednesday
Rotation from semiconductors into healthcare, industrials, and software — Dow +1% vs Nasdaq -0.2%

stocks.discussion_driver: Amkor beat Q2 2026 estimates handily (EPS $0.70 vs $0.45 est, revenue $1.9B vs $1.81B) but issued disappointing Q3 revenue guidance, triggering a brutal 24% single-day selloff. A recently announced NVIDIA partnership underscores long-term AI packaging demand, but near-term guidance uncertainty has spooked investors and the stock is now 52% below its 52-week high.
bull_case: NVIDIA partnership highlights growing AI advanced packaging demand; Amkor is positioned as a critical outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) player for AI chiplets
Q2 2026 EPS of $0.70 beat estimates of $0.45 by 56%, demonstrating strong operational execution despite a challenging macro backdrop
bear_case: Q3 2026 revenue guidance came in below Wall Street consensus, triggering a 24% single-day share collapse and raising questions about forward demand visibility
Broad chip sector sell-off from CXMT supply glut fears amplifies individual guidance disappointment; packaging demand could soften if AI chip production slows

stocks.discussion_driver: Micron slid ~9.8% as the global chip sell-off deepened following CXMT's 466% IPO debut (China DRAM maker) and SK Hynix's 15% single-day crash in South Korea, fueling fears of a DRAM supply glut. Despite sector headwinds, Micron's HBM leadership for AI data centers, RSI near oversold territory, and a 35% discount to its 52-week high make it one of the most compelling value setups in the semiconductor space.
bull_case: HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) for AI data centers is a high-margin secular growth driver; Micron is one of only three global suppliers alongside Samsung and SK Hynix
RSI near 38 (oversold territory) and a 35% discount to 52-week high combined with 45-analyst Strong Buy consensus at $1,492 average target suggest significant mean-reversion upside
bear_case: CXMT's 466% IPO debut signals massive new Chinese DRAM capacity entering the global market, raising credible fears of a prolonged supply glut that could compress DRAM pricing
SK Hynix's 15% single-day crash in South Korea signals global memory sector panic; commodity memory pricing could deteriorate faster than HBM premiums can offset

stocks.discussion_driver: AMD fell 8%+ as the semiconductor sector rout from CXMT's IPO and SK Hynix's crash pushed the Nasdaq-100 into correction territory. Despite broad chip sector headwinds, AMD's AI accelerator business remains a core growth driver with shares still up over 100% YTD. Big Tech earnings this week (MSFT, AMZN, AAPL, META) and the Fed decision Wednesday could reignite AI spending sentiment and serve as near-term catalysts.
bull_case: AMD's MI300 AI GPU series is gaining data center market share; Baird raised its price target to $1,250 (Outperform) reflecting transformative AI accelerator revenue growth potential
Shares have more than doubled in 2026 YTD and the 8%+ pullback on sector-wide macro fears—not AMD-specific fundamentals—creates a tactical buying opportunity ahead of Big Tech earnings
bear_case: Chip sector rout from CXMT IPO and SK Hynix crash creates broad semiconductor headwinds regardless of AMD's AI merit; near-term price action likely remains volatile
Trailing P/E of 162x is extremely stretched even for a high-growth AI company; any earnings miss or guidance cut could trigger severe multiple compression

stocks.discussion_driver: Corning plunged 16-17% despite reporting a solid Q2 beat (EPS $0.78 vs $0.76 est, GAAP revenue $4.51B, +17% YoY), as Q3 revenue guidance disappointed Wall Street. The stock is now 47% below its 52-week high yet analysts maintain a Buy consensus with a $215.47 target—implying 50% upside—based on optical fiber demand from AI data center buildout and strong execution across its enterprise and carrier markets.
bull_case: Optical fiber and data center connectivity demand from AI infrastructure buildout provides a multi-year secular tailwind for Corning's core businesses
Q2 GAAP revenue +17% YoY demonstrates strong underlying demand; analyst consensus Buy with $215 average target implies 50% upside from post-earnings lows
bear_case: Q3 guidance miss triggered a 16-17% single-day selloff despite a Q2 beat—management credibility and forward revenue visibility are now under scrutiny
Down 27% over the past week and 47% below its 52-week high, the stock faces potential further selling as momentum investors exit and guidance uncertainty lingers

stocks.discussion_driver: Teradyne surged 14% in after-hours trading on July 28 after reporting a massive Q2 2026 beat—EPS $2.47 vs $2.06 consensus (20% beat) and revenue $1.33B vs $1.22B estimate (+104% YoY growth). Q3 guidance midpoint of $1.25B also topped the $1.03B consensus. Despite the after-hours pop, the regular July 28 close of $321.07 remains 34% below TER's 52-week high, representing a potential re-rating opportunity as AI-driven chip complexity accelerates test equipment demand.
bull_case: Q2 revenue surged 104% YoY with EPS beating by 20% and Q3 guidance well above estimates, confirming an AI-driven semiconductor test equipment supercycle is underway
Post-earnings analyst price target upgrades (Cantor $550, BofA $525, Susquehanna $550, UBS $500) imply 55-71% upside from the July 28 close
bear_case: Stock is 34% below its June 2026 52-week high with a 23% pullback over the past month, reflecting sustained chip sector selling pressure even for outperforming companies
After-hours surge of 14% may face profit-taking as the broader semiconductor sector remains under pressure from supply glut fears and Korea market contagion
